Posted November 30, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan Sponsored by Advanced Nutrients.
See
 Two BC Growers Bag Cannabis Cup Prizes. Dutch Growers Face Competition and Government Harassment. Spain Looks Warmer. Reporting from Amsterdam.

As best I recall, I have been in Amsterdam for six of the seventeen Cannabis Cups, but I have never really taken part in most of the activities. In the early 90s, when I was National Director of NORML, I was there to show our gratitude for High Times support for NORML. However, the truth is that I really just go to see old friends. (Really, honest.) Consequently, I am not the best person to evaluate the event.

Frankly, I don't think that the Cup is the best way to see Amsterdam, partly because the weather there can be nasty in late November. This year it was a bit worse than usual, but if someone is coming from the Northeastern states or from anywhere in Canada, outside of BC, that won't be a problem.

Also, the most popular coffee shops are very crowded during the Cup. Nonetheless, real cannabis aficionados should try to do it once and decide for themselves. That said, there are a few things (and people) that visitors might overlook and Americans in particular should try to see whenever they visit.

The latest data from the 2004 report from The European Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Drug Addiction (EMCDDA) once again demonstrate that the Dutch cannabis policies are much more successful than prohibition. MarijuanaNews will have a complete report soon.
